images.seen: Ming, Later Jin, Joseon, Mongol Khanate and the Tumed disc at Hohhot look sound; the Tumed disc spills over northern Shanxi (patched); the thin Ming Liaoxi strip and the Mongol Khanate's inland Liaoning are plausible, left.

Wrong: Mosul (Ninawa 148 cells) and Dihok/Arbil are nobody's grey wedge, Basra is Safavid, and a 74-cell grey hole at Kandahar sits on the Mughal border; Cliopatria shows none of these because it paints Safavid over the wedge.

Europe reads right: Swedish Livonia and Estonia as Swedish colonies, Duchy of Livonia gone after Altmark, Lusatia occupation hatching, Danish phase and Thirty Years' War contests plausible; small size-rule leftovers only.
Wrong: the Saadi Sultanate is drawn as a 1,600-cell tentacle through the Sahara to the Niger bend, 1618-1628, although direct control of the Sudan ended in 1618 (patched).
After the patch the Saadi are Morocco only, with the Timbuktu pashalik circles as vassals; no tentacle.
After the patch Mosul and Basra are Ottoman and the Kandahar hole is closed; Dihok and Arbil stay nobody's (pages silent).

issues.what: Saadi Sultanate keeps the whole Saharan corridor and Niger bend (about 1,600 cells) as direct land from 1618 until the 1629 keyframe snap removes 1,608 cells at once; its own keyframe 1612 says Morocco alone for 1618-1628.

Iraq in 1626: the Cliopatria shapes of Ottoman and Safavid both leave out Mosul (Ninawa 148 cells), so it became nobody's land after being Safavid in 1625; Basra (68 cells) stayed Safavid although the Persians 'retreated from Basra' in 1624; the Ottoman army 'withdrew to Mosul' on 4 July 1626. The snap order (Ottoman keyframe first, Safavid second) lost the Ottoman claim to the size rule, so a ruling was needed besides the keyframe overrides.
Kandahar: the Safavid 1626 shape holds 123 of the province's 197 cells, so the snap turned 74 Registan cells into nobody's grey hole on the Mughal border.

Tumed (200 km disc round Hohhot) beats the Ming by the size rule on 105 Shanxi and 9 Shaanxi cells inside the Ming border (402 cell-years); the Altan Khan page puts the Tumed pastures 'north of the border with Shanxi'. A ruling alone could not act in 1620-1621 (no claim), so a Ming gain event from the Tumed gives the cells for the whole window; the ruling written first settled nothing afterwards and was dropped.

Ya'rubid keyframe 1626 never applied: its dossier correction names 'Julfar', which the gazetteer lacks, so the Ya'rubids held only the Nizwa disc and then (conflict) Muscat and Sohar against the Portuguese. Julfar replaced by the Ras al Khaymah place (the Julfar page: 'a predecessor settlement to Ras Al Khaimah').

Ming / Mongol Khanate (435 cell-years, Liaoning 219 cells) and Later Jin / Ming (R2): the Chahar shape claims inland Liaoxi and the Ming keep only a thin Ningyuan-Jinzhou strip; plausible, no page opened.

Matamba / Kasanje contest of 118 cells opens in 1620 (matamba ledger 1) and has no contest_end until the 1631 rename: a contested zone that never ends in this window. The Kasanje page dates only the 1620 attack and wars of 1634-5.

Dihok (22) and Arbil (46) cells are nobody's land from 1626, and Kirkuk (32) stays Safavid; the pages say 'most of Iraq, including Kirkuk and Mosul' were taken in 1624-1625 and give no later changes there.

Smaller size-rule results: Iberian Union / France in Franche-Comté (35 cell-years, France wins), Savoy / French royal domain (26, 1620), Electoral Palatinate / Iberian Union (71, Palatinate wins although Spanish troops held the Lower Palatinate; the occupation events are in the dossiers), Duchy of Livonia / Swedish Empire 1622 (178, Duchy wins, plausible before the Swedish gains of 1625). Not worth a page each.
Skipped VOC events of 1621 (ledger 5 and 6, Banda): the islands have no land cell in the resolution-5 grid, so no patch can place them.
